relations.subject: Yu Ying-shih
relations.evidence: He was the elder brother of philosopher, educator, and university president Paul Yu.

relations.subject: Yu Ying-shih
relations.evidence: In 1949, he enrolled in Yenching University, but shortly came to Hong Kong for reunion with his family.

relations.subject: Yu Ying-shih
relations.evidence: He then studied in the newly founded New Asia College, later incorporated into Chinese University of Hong Kong... and became the first graduate of the college.

relations.subject: Yu Ying-shih
relations.evidence: Yu studied with Ch'ien Mu, a scholar rooted in traditional Chinese philosophy, and became the first graduate of the college.

relations.subject: Yu Ying-shih
relations.evidence: Yu came to Harvard University in the United States to pursue his PhD in Chinese history.

relations.subject: Yu Ying-shih
relations.evidence: He then taught at various universities including University of Michigan, Harvard, Yale University and Princeton University.

relations.subject: Yu Ying-shih
relations.evidence: He was a tenured professor at Harvard University and Yale University before his time at Princeton.

relations.subject: Yu Ying-shih
relations.role: Head of college and Pro Vice-Chancellor of University
relations.evidence: In 1973, he went back to his alma mater, New Asia College, as its Head of college and also the Pro Vice-Chancellor of University for two years, before returning to Harvard.

relations.subject: Yu Ying-shih
relations.role: Charles Seymour Professor in Chinese History
relations.evidence: In 1977, he moved to Yale to take up the position of Charles Seymour Professor in Chinese History. He then moved to Princeton in 1987

relations.subject: Yu Ying-shih
relations.evidence: He then moved to Princeton in 1987 to be Professor of East Asian Studies until his retirement... He retired from Princeton in 2001.

relations.subject: Yu Ying-shih
relations.evidence: In 1974, he was elected as a Fellow at Academia Sinica, and has kept this position until his death.
